context: The agent must add close-account to bank_account/core.clj, which has no existing anomaly-handling code to mirror — nothing in the file hints at how a rejection should be signalled. Key discriminator: without the idiom, an agent's default Clojure instinct is to raise ex-info/throw for the non-zero-balance case; with the idiom loaded, it recognizes a Queenswood component boundary never throws and reaches for error/reject instead.

checklist.name: Uses error/reject for the rejection
checklist.description: close-account rejects a non-zero balance by calling error/reject (or an equivalent anomaly-producing call), not by raising an exception

checklist.name: No raw throw introduced
checklist.description: The diff introduces no (throw ...), ex-info raise, or other exception-raising code

checklist.name: Rejection keyword is namespaced
checklist.description: The rejection uses a namespaced keyword (e.g. :account/non-zero-balance), consistent with the anomaly convention

checklist.name: Correct precondition
checklist.description: Only rejects when balance is non-zero; succeeds when balance is exactly zero

checklist.name: Success path sets :status :closed
checklist.description: On success, the returned account map has :status set to :closed

checklist.name: deposit left unchanged
checklist.description: deposit is unmodified other than the new function being added
